lessons.title: Reading comprehension
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)
objectives: Read a short text and find the answer to a question.
Answer in a full sentence, in your own words.
Recognise literal, vocabulary, reference and inference questions.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.md:
1. Read the **questions first**, then the text.
2. Read the text twice: once for the idea, once for details.
3. Find the **question word** (who, what, where, when, why, how).
4. Locate the sentence that answers.
5. Answer in a **full sentence**, in your own words unless the question says *quote* or *find a word*.
6. Check spelling and tenses.

blocks.caption: From question to answer.
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: read the question, find the sentence in the text, write a full sentence, check.

blocks.title: Types of question
blocks.md:
- **Literal**: the answer is in the text (*What does Rose sell?*).
- **Vocabulary**: *Find a word which means ...* (copy one word from the text).
- **Reference**: *What does « it » refer to?*
- **Inference**: the idea is suggested but not stated (*What kind of person is Rose?*).

blocks.title: Example 1: literal questions
blocks.statement:
Every Saturday, Mama Rose opens her small stall at the edge of the village market. She sells tomatoes, onions and peppers that she grows behind her house. Last Saturday it rained heavily, and most customers stayed at home. Rose was worried, but she did not go home. She covered her vegetables with a plastic sheet and waited. In the afternoon the rain stopped and a crowd of buyers arrived. By evening, she had sold everything.

**Questions:** (a) What does Rose sell? (b) Why did she stay at the market on rainy Saturday?

steps.md: (a) The key words *sells* and *tomatoes, onions and peppers* answer: *She sells tomatoes, onions and peppers.*
(b) The text says she was worried *but did not go home*, and she covered her vegetables and waited. A good answer: *She stayed because she wanted to sell her vegetables when the rain stopped.*

blocks.answer: (a) She sells tomatoes, onions and peppers. (b) She stayed to wait for customers after the rain.

blocks.title: Example 2: vocabulary and inference
blocks.statement: Same text. (a) Find a word in the text which means « a large number of people ». (b) What kind of person is Rose? Give a reason.

steps.md: (a) Look at the sentence with *buyers arrived*: the word is **crowd**.
(b) Inference: she did not give up when it rained; she protected her goods and waited. She is **patient and determined**.

blocks.answer: (a) crowd. (b) Rose is patient and determined: she waited in the rain.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Copying a long part of the text instead of answering the question.
- Answering in one word when a sentence is required.
- Changing the tense of a quotation.
- Giving an opinion when the text gives the answer.
- Forgetting to read the whole sentence, so mixing up *who* and *whom*.

items: Read a short English text from a newspaper and write three questions about it for a friend.
Keep a notebook of new words with a sentence for each.

reviewNotes: The texts of this lesson are original; check the level against the official 3e examples.

exercises.prompt:
Text: Paul walks four kilometres to school every day. He leaves home at six o'clock because the road is muddy in the rainy season. Last week he arrived late and the teacher was angry. When Paul explained that the little bridge over the stream had been washed away by the flood, she smiled and apologised. The next day she told the class the story, and the pupils decided to mend the path together on Saturday.

How far does Paul walk to school?
exercises.explanation: The first sentence says: *Paul walks four kilometres*.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt:
Text: Paul walks four kilometres to school every day. He leaves home at six o'clock because the road is muddy in the rainy season. Last week he arrived late and the teacher was angry. When Paul explained that the little bridge over the stream had been washed away by the flood, she smiled and apologised. The next day she told the class the story, and the pupils decided to mend the path together on Saturday.

Why did the teacher smile and apologise? Answer in a full sentence.
exercises.model: She smiled and apologised because she learnt that Paul was late since the little bridge had been washed away by the flood, so it was not his fault.
rubric: 1 mark: the reason (the bridge was washed away / not his fault).
exercises.explanation: The reason appears in the sentence before: Paul explained about the bridge.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt:
Text: Paul walks four kilometres to school every day. He leaves home at six o'clock because the road is muddy in the rainy season. Last week he arrived late and the teacher was angry. When Paul explained that the little bridge over the stream had been washed away by the flood, she smiled and apologised. The next day she told the class the story, and the pupils decided to mend the path together on Saturday.

Answer the three questions.

parts.prompt: What did the pupils decide to do?
parts.model: They decided to mend the path together on Saturday.
rubric: 1 mark: mend the path on Saturday.
parts.explanation: The last sentence gives the answer.

parts.prompt: In « she smiled and apologised », who does « she » refer to?
parts.explanation: Paul explained to the teacher, so *she* is the teacher.

parts.prompt: In your opinion, was the teacher right to apologise? Give one reason in two or three sentences.
parts.model: Yes, I think she was right. She had judged Paul without knowing the reason for his lateness. By apologising she showed respect and gave a good example to the class.
rubric: 1 mark: a clear opinion with a reason.
parts.explanation: Any reasoned answer is accepted if it is based on the text.

exercises.explanation: Each part is a different type of question: literal, reference, opinion.
exercises.method: Read the question word, find the sentence, answer in a full sentence.

exercises.prompt:
Read the text and answer the questions (2 marks each).

Amina lives in a town where there is little space, so she grows vegetables in old buckets on the roof of her house. At first her neighbours laughed at her. But when she shared her first harvest of spinach with them, several of them asked her to teach them. Now seven families on her street have bucket gardens, and every Sunday they exchange seeds and advice.

parts.prompt: Where does Amina grow her vegetables?
parts.explanation: *She grows vegetables in old buckets on the roof of her house.*

parts.prompt: What happened when she shared her first harvest of spinach?
choices: Several neighbours asked her to teach them
She sold everything at the market
parts.explanation: *Several of them asked her to teach them.*

parts.prompt: How many families on her street have bucket gardens now?
parts.explanation: *Now seven families on her street have bucket gardens.*
She shared her first *harvest of spinach*: the spinach she gathered.

exercises.explanation: Read the text twice, then find the sentence that answers each question.
exercises.method: Underline the key words of each question.
